metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Greece strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, have you thought about getting a bottle of champagne for Adam's party? It seems like a nice gesture to celebrate his scholarship. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... I don't know if champagne is the best choice. It's not really the way we celebrate in Greece. Maybe something more personal, like a nice pen or a book that inspired me? That feels more meaningful to me. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, celebrating achievements like this is done with champagne. It shows excitement and support. Your idea of a pen or a book doesn’t really capture the moment. It feels... well, kind of backward. We celebrate big wins with something special, you know? It's how it works. Making a big deal out of it is important.

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand that you see it that way, but in Greece, making a personal gesture carries a lot of weight too. I just think that something thoughtful like a pen or a book might express my pride more. I want to honor Adam's achievement in a way that feels true to my values. It’s not about being backward; it’s about being meaningful.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I get that you want to be meaningful, but isn’t there a way to blend both? Like, get the champagne to celebrate and maybe add a personal note or a small gift? It’s not just about showing pride; it's about celebrating together. We can honor Adam in a big way and still keep your thoughtful touch. And about making our parents proud— isn’t that something we should also consider in our choices?

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: Blending both could work, I guess... But for me, making my parents proud is central to how I choose to honor my friends. They’ve always taught me to value personal connections over grand gestures. If I do a small gift with a thoughtful note, it’s my way of showing that I care deeply. It's about the values I want to uphold, not just the celebration itself. Isn’t it important to stay true to what means the most for us?
